topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The subtopic establishes the lecture framing, course context, and core learning objectives for cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the principles, systemic toxicities, and drug-efflux resistance mechanisms associated with local interventions and cytotoxic chemotherapy.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer-specific defects and pathway vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on therapeutic strategies designed to exploit intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities, including hormone dependency, checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair.

topics.label: Kinase-targeted therapies and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine small-molecule inhibition of hyperactivated oncogenic kinases alongside the mutational, bypass, and paradoxical activation mechanisms driving drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody and antibody-drug conjugate therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how targeted antibody platforms are engineered to block receptor signaling or deliver cytotoxic payloads directly to tumor cells.

topics.label: Immune surveillance and cancer immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of immune surveillance and the clinical modalities used to re-engage T cells against tumors.

topics.label: Clinical progress, persistent dilemmas, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate historical trends in cancer survival and discuss ongoing challenges regarding heterogeneity, clinical trial ethics, and future treatment paradigms.
